punchline: A random spin of a wheel shifted people's estimates by twenty percentage points.
thirty_sec: Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky rigged a wheel to stop at 10 or 65, then asked students what percentage of UN members were African nations. Those who saw 10 guessed 25 percent; those who saw 65 guessed 45. Even German judges gave longer sentences after rolling rigged dice showing 9 rather than 3. The anchoring effect works on experts too, often without them noticing.
question: Who set the anchor in your last negotiation, you or the other side?
